name: Genetics foundations
intro: The vocabulary that everything else is built on: genes, chromosomes, alleles, transcription and translation, inheritance patterns and the chemistry of nucleic acids.

name: Human and population genomics
intro: How genetic variation is distributed within and between human populations, and the concepts used to study it: allele frequency, linkage disequilibrium, ancestry, association studies and reference resources.

name: Clinical and cancer genomics
intro: Terminology used when genomic information informs diagnosis, screening and cancer care, including variant classification, penetrance, tumour evolution and the limits of what a genomic result can establish.

name: Pathogen genomics
intro: Sequencing and analysis of bacteria, viruses, fungi and parasites for outbreak investigation, antimicrobial resistance surveillance and public health decision-making.

name: Sequencing and laboratory methods
intro: How genomic data is produced: extraction, library preparation, sequencing chemistries and platforms, quality control and the measurements that describe a run.

name: Bioinformatics and statistics
intro: File formats, alignment, assembly, variant calling, workflows and reproducibility, together with the statistical ideas needed to interpret genomic results honestly.

name: Pharmacogenomics
intro: How inherited variation affects the way medicines are processed and tolerated, the nomenclature used to describe it, and the guidelines that translate genotype into prescribing advice.

name: Ethics and data governance
intro: Consent, data sharing, access control, equitable partnership and the legal and ethical frameworks that govern genomic data and samples.
